concepts.note: Coulomb's torsion balance measured tiny electrostatic forces by balancing them against a twisted fiber.
concepts.title: Torsion balance

concepts.note: The electrostatic force decreases with the square of the separation, establishing the first quantitative law of electricity.
concepts.title: Inverse-square law

concepts.note: The net force on a charge is the vector sum of the forces from individual charges.
concepts.title: Superposition of charges

subtopics.note: Coulomb used a torsion balance to show that the force between point charges is proportional to q₁q₂ and falls off as 1/r²: F = (1/4πε₀) q₁q₂/r².
subtopics.title: Coulomb's law

concepts.note: Young observed interference between light passing through two nearby slits, a signature of wave superposition.
concepts.title: Double-slit experiment

concepts.note: Bright and dark bands arise from constructive and destructive superposition of light waves.
concepts.title: Interference fringes

concepts.note: Overlapping light waves add amplitudes, so their relative phase determines the resulting intensity.
concepts.title: Principle of superposition

concepts.note: Young's results challenged Newton's corpuscular theory and reopened the question of light's nature.
concepts.title: Wave–particle debate

subtopics.note: Young's interference experiments revived the wave theory by showing that light from two slits produces alternating bright and dark fringes with spacing Δy = λL/d.
subtopics.title: Wave theory of light

concepts.note: In 1820 Ørsted found that a current-carrying wire deflects a nearby magnetic compass needle.
concepts.title: Ørsted's compass experiment

concepts.note: The line integral of magnetic field around a closed loop equals μ₀ times the enclosed current.
concepts.title: Ampère's circuital law

concepts.note: Parallel currents attract when in the same direction and repel when opposite.
concepts.title: Parallel-current forces

concepts.note: Ampère's integro-differential law gives the force between infinitesimal current elements, later superseded by field theory.
concepts.title: Current-element force law

subtopics.note: Ampère explained Ørsted's 1820 observation of a magnetic needle deflected by current and formulated the force law between current-carrying wires, with F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πr) for parallel wires.
subtopics.title: Ampère's force law

concepts.note: Relative motion of a magnet and coil or a changing current generates a transient current in the coil.
concepts.title: Electromagnetic induction

concepts.note: Flux Φ_B is the surface integral of B, and its rate of change determines the induced EMF.
concepts.title: Magnetic flux

concepts.note: Faraday introduced intuitive field lines to describe magnetic and electric action through space.
concepts.title: Lines of force

concepts.note: The homopolar generator produced a continuous current from a rotating conducting disk in a magnetic field.
concepts.title: Faraday disk

subtopics.note: Faraday found that a changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an electromotive force, ε = −dΦ_B/dt, linking magnetism and electricity.
subtopics.title: Faraday induction

concepts.note: A changing electric field acts as a current source of magnetic field, making Ampère's law consistent with charge conservation.
concepts.title: Displacement current

concepts.note: Gauss's laws, Faraday's law and the Ampère–Maxwell law relate E, B, charge and current.
concepts.title: Four field equations

concepts.note: Maxwell identified light as a propagating oscillation of electric and magnetic fields.
concepts.title: Electromagnetic theory of light

concepts.note: Maxwell's waves were initially thought to propagate through a mechanical aether, later discarded.
concepts.title: Luminiferous aether

subtopics.note: Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and optics in four field equations, adding displacement current so that ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t and predicting c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀).
subtopics.title: Maxwell equations

concepts.note: A high-voltage spark drove oscillating currents in a dipole-like antenna, radiating electromagnetic waves.
concepts.title: Spark-gap oscillator

concepts.note: A small loop with a spark gap detected the arriving waves by resonant induction.
concepts.title: Resonant receiver loop

concepts.note: Hertz showed that the waves could be reflected, refracted and polarized like light.
concepts.title: Reflection and polarization

concepts.note: Hertz used standing waves to measure the wavelength and inferred a speed close to that of light.
concepts.title: Speed-of-light measurement

subtopics.note: Hertz generated and detected radio waves with spark-gap apparatus, confirming Maxwell's prediction that light is an electromagnetic wave travelling at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀).
subtopics.title: Electromagnetic waves

concepts.note: The electric term qE accelerates a charge while the magnetic term qv×B acts perpendicular to velocity.
concepts.title: Force on moving charge

concepts.note: In a uniform magnetic field the Lorentz force produces circular or helical motion with cyclotron frequency qB/m.
concepts.title: Charged-particle trajectories

concepts.note: Lorentz treated matter as composed of charged particles whose motion produced electromagnetic phenomena.
concepts.title: Electron theory of matter

subtopics.note: Lorentz formulated the force on a charge moving in electric and magnetic fields, F = q(E + v×B), completing the classical dynamics of charged particles.
subtopics.title: Lorentz force law
